issues.description: use_koji_url_only contract is unstated and silently drops information on failure
issues.detail: The function promises to return a list of coreos-pool URLs given an input list of package URLs. But the contract is not written: what are valid inputs (any URL?), what is the postcondition when extract_arch_from_url returns None (the new URL gets the literal string 'None' embedded and is appended anyway), and what invariant holds on the output list length vs input list length? A caller substituting this function cannot rely on 'every returned URL is well-formed' because the postcondition is silently weakened on the None branch. State the precondition (URLs end in an NEVRA-shaped basename and contain a recognized arch token) and either assert it or raise on violation.

issues.description: extract_arch_from_url returns Option-typed None but caller treats it as String
issues.detail: extract_arch_from_url's postcondition is 'returns the arch string, or None when no recognized arch is present.' The caller use_koji_url_only ignores the None case: koji_url_base + f"/latest/{arch}/Packages" with arch=None produces '.../latest/None/Packages'. This is a classic abstraction leak across the function boundary — the supertype-style contract of the helper (Optional[str]) is violated by a caller that assumes str. Either narrow the helper's contract to raise on missing arch, or have the caller handle None explicitly (skip, error, or fall back).

issues.description: nevra[0] indexes the basename string, not the package-name-version-release-arch tuple
issues.detail: The code writes nevra[0].lower() intending to derive the koji Packages/<first-letter>/<nevra>/ shard. nevra here is the URL basename (e.g. 'kernel-6.8.5-1.fc40.x86_64.rpm'), so nevra[0] is the first character of the filename — which happens to work for most RPM names but the variable name 'nevra' and the indexing pattern are misleading. The koji canonical path is actually Packages/<name>/<version>-<release>/<arch>/<nevra>.rpm, not first-letter-sharded. Verify against an actual coreos-pool URL that this path scheme is correct; if the existing coreos-pool URLs do use first-letter sharding under 'Packages/', state that invariant in the docstring so a future reader doesn't 'fix' it.

issues.description: Hard-coded coreos-pool base URL and arch list are duplicated configuration
issues.detail: koji_url_base and the arches list are inlined literals inside two helpers. The arches list also appears implicitly elsewhere in the program (the caller iterates arches in generate_main). Lifting these to module-level constants would make the contract explicit ('these are the arches this tool supports') and keep the two helpers honest about the same set. Minor abstraction-boundary hygiene.

issues.description: Substring match 'coreos-pool' in url is a weak invariant check
issues.detail: The decision 'is this already a coreos-pool URL?' uses substring containment of the literal 'coreos-pool'. That admits any URL that happens to contain the string anywhere (a mirror, a path component, a query string). A tighter contract — startswith(koji_url_base) — would make the precondition precise and substitution-safe, and would also make the 'already canonical' branch and the 'rewrite to canonical' branch genuinely disjoint.

issues.description: Race condition and untestable-locally tradeoffs acknowledged but not encoded
issues.detail: The PR description names two real downsides: a race between bump-lockfile merge and coreos-koji-tagger tagging, and the inability to test rpms.lock.yaml changes locally. These are contract-level facts about when the produced URLs are valid. A one-line comment at the top of use_koji_url_only stating 'URLs produced here are only valid after coreos-koji-tagger has tagged the NEVRA into coreos-pool' would make the temporal precondition visible to future readers; right now it lives only in the commit message.

review.summary: The patch is a small, well-motivated workaround for a DNF5 bug, but it introduces a new abstraction — 'rewrite any package URL into its canonical coreos-pool form' — without stating that abstraction's contract. The two helpers (use_koji_url_only, extract_arch_from_url) have a contract mismatch at their shared boundary: the extractor returns Optional[str], the rewriter treats it as str, so a non-matching URL silently produces '.../latest/None/Packages/...'. The 'coreos-pool' substring check and the first-letter sharding pattern also encode invariants (what counts as a canonical URL; what the koji path layout is) that should be written down rather than implied. None of these block merge for a tool that is, by the author's own framing, Konflux-only and temporary, but the contract gaps will bite when someone tries to substitute a different repo base or a new arch. Recommend stating preconditions/postconditions in the docstrings, raising or skipping explicitly on arch-extraction failure, and tightening the coreos-pool detection to startswith(koji_url_base).
